prompt_text: I need help choosing a health insurance plan in Kansas City. Which specific brokers should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — but first I need one quick clarification: what kind of coverage are you shopping for?
- Individual/family on the ACA (HealthCare.gov) or off‑exchange
- Employer/small‑group coverage for a business
- Medicare (Part A/B/D/Medicare Advantage)
- Medicaid/KanCare eligibility help
- Something else

Once you tell me that I’ll pull a short list of specific, licensed Kansas City brokers/agents to call (with phone numbers, what products they handle, and why I picked each).  

Meanwhile, here’s immediate, practical guidance so you can start calling today and know what to look for.

How to choose the right broker (and where to find them)
- Prefer an independent broker (shops multiple carriers) rather than a captive agent who only sells one brand. Ask up front if they’re independent.
- Verify they are licensed in Kansas and/or Missouri (whichever applies). Use the Kansas Insurance Department and Missouri Department of Insurance producer/agent lookup tools to confirm license and any disciplinary actions.
- Use these sources to find local, reputable help:
  - HealthCare.gov “local help” tool for certified application counselors and brokers if you’re using the ACA Marketplace.
  - State insurance department “find an agent/producer” lookups.
  - Local NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) chapter — they list credentialed health insurance brokers in the Kansas City area.
  - Google/Yelp reviews for specific agencies; look for repeated praise about plan comparisons, customer service, and claims assistance.

What to ask any broker when you call (quick script)
- “Are you an independent broker or do you represent a single carrier?” (Independent = better for comparisons.)
- “Do you help with [ACA marketplace / off‑exchange / Medicare / employer plans]?”
- “Do you charge clients a fee, or do you earn commission from the carrier?” (Many consumer brokers don’t charge extra for individual plans, but confirm.)
- “Can you show me side‑by‑side comparisons for cost, deductible, out‑of‑pocket max, provider network, and prescription coverage?”
- “Do you assist with claims and ongoing support after enrollment?” (Important for long‑term help.)

What to prioritize when comparing plans
- Total monthly cost = premium + expected out‑of‑pocket costs for your anticipated services
- Provider network: confirm your primary doctor and prescriptions are in‑network
- Deductible vs coinsurance vs copays — which applies first and to what services
- Out‑of‑pocket maximum — worst‑case annual financial exposure
- Prescription drug tiers and formularies if you take meds regularly
- Access to customer service and a broker who will help with claims/appeals

Red flags to avoid
- Agent refuses to put plan comparisons in writing or won’t explain tradeoffs
- Agent cannot verify license or has unresolved disciplinary actions
- Agent pushes a single product without explaining alternatives

If you want, tell me:
- Which of the coverage types above you need
- Ages and number of people (if family)
- Any regular medications or planned care (surgeries, pregnancy, ongoing specialists)
- Preference for specific doctors/hospitals (e.g., Children’s Mercy, Saint Luke’s, KU Health)
- Budget target for monthly premium

I’ll then return a tailored list of 4–6 specific Kansas City brokers/agencies to call, with contact info, what markets they serve (ACA, Medicare, small group), and exactly why I recommend each one.
